transcriptionNote: All 150 printed question numbers have been aligned to the uploaded 20-page Series I booklet. A missing Q117 (wound watch spring) was restored and the previous one-place numbering shift from Q117 onward was corrected. Source scan corrections: Q61 Punctilious, Q62 Mendacious, Q76 Jital, Q131 HOTEL=12, Q133 train speed 60 km/h, Q143 equation 8*8*1*7=8 and operator options, Q150 powers 2²⁵⁰, 3¹⁵⁰, 5¹⁰⁰, 4²⁰⁰. Answered items are independently solved, not official-key answers. Q7, Q9, Q10, Q14, Q16, Q25, Q26, Q111 and Q141 remain explicitly unresolved; no guesses have been inserted.

questions.text: Hippopotamus loves to wallow in ____ mud.
questions.explanation: “Mud” is an uncountable noun used generally here, so it takes no article.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: The Principal welcomed the students ____ the school.
questions.explanation: The verb “welcome” takes “to” when naming the destination: welcome someone to the school.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: I love having ____ eggs for breakfast.
questions.explanation: The plural noun “eggs” is used generically, so no article is needed.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: I have ____ of things on my mind.
questions.explanation: “A lot of” is the natural quantifier before the plural count noun “things”.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: The members of the choir ____ every Saturday.
questions.explanation: “Members” is plural, so the present-simple verb is “meet”.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: The Aryans are ____ European stock.
questions.explanation: The standard expression is “of European stock,” indicating ancestry or origin.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: John was ____ at the surprising turn of events.
questions.explanation: Both “surprised” and “amazed” are grammatically and semantically possible with “at”; the sentence does not uniquely distinguish them.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: Such a gruesome event ____ never happened in the locality before.
questions.explanation: “An event has never happened” uses the present perfect to describe experience up to now.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: Cleopatra was said to be an ____ beauty in her time.
questions.explanation: “Incomparable”, “unparalleled”, “outstanding” and “unmatched” can all describe beauty here. The options do not yield one defensible unique answer.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: The delegates ____ since morning to meet the CEO.
questions.explanation: The natural tense is “have been waiting since morning”, but that option is absent. None of the printed alternatives completes the sentence correctly.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: The divers dived deep ____ the sea to locate the ship.
questions.explanation: “Into the sea” expresses movement from the surface to a position inside the sea.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: By the time the concert ended, the children ____ already asleep.
questions.explanation: The past perfect “had been” places the children’s state of being asleep before the concert ended.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: Despite ____, the Judge was moved to pity.
questions.explanation: “Despite his hard-heartedness” contrasts his lack of sympathy with the judge’s eventual pity.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: The girls cheered ____ when their team scored a goal.
questions.explanation: Both “loudly” and “wildly” can naturally describe cheering; no context makes one uniquely correct.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: You've understood, ____?
questions.explanation: The positive statement “You have understood” takes the negative question tag “haven’t you?”
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: Neither of the candidates ____ for the debate.
questions.explanation: Both present (“shows up”) and past (“showed up”) can be grammatical depending on the intended time reference, which is not supplied.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: ____ and lodging are available here.
questions.explanation: The established expression is “food and lodging.”
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: Walking ____ the best way to stay fit.
questions.explanation: A gerund phrase used as the subject takes a singular verb: “Walking is…”
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: Because of global warming, the climate ____ changed a lot.
questions.explanation: “Has changed” is present perfect, describing a change from the past with relevance to the present.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: Democracy without freedom is ____.
questions.explanation: Without freedom, democracy loses its essential meaning; “meaningless” completes the sentence.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: He was so passionate about the job, he was like ____.
questions.explanation: “A man on a mission” describes someone strongly driven by a purpose, matching the context of passion.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: Who ____ to apply for the post of Treasurer?
questions.explanation: “Who” is the subject of the singular verb “wants” in this question.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: We can eat in the café ____ order a takeout.
questions.explanation: “Or” connects the two alternatives: eating at the café or ordering takeout.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: She succeeded ____ everyone failed.
questions.explanation: “Where” introduces the contrasting circumstance/place in which she succeeded while others failed.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: Choose the word that best completes the source sentence: ____.
questions.explanation: The source prompt/sentence is absent or illegible in the uploaded scan; the item cannot be reconstructed without guessing.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: She could not convince the jury ____ her pleas.
questions.explanation: Both “by her pleas” and “with her pleas” can describe the means of persuasion; the options do not distinguish them.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: Please don't walk ____ the grass.
questions.explanation: The standard collocation is “walk on the grass.”
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: Good heavens! How time ____.
questions.explanation: “How time flies!” is the fixed exclamation expressing how quickly time passes.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: Her job comes with a ____ pay package.
questions.explanation: “Hefty” means large or substantial, commonly used to describe a generous pay package.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: Jim was already in bed when I ____ him last night.
questions.explanation: “Last night” sets a past time; the completed action is expressed by “called.”
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: Choose the correct sentences: (i) The bulldozer made a humming noise. (ii) The noise irritated people nearby. (iii) They complained against the irritated bulldozer.
questions.explanation: Statements (i) and (ii) are grammatically sound. Statement (iii) wrongly describes the bulldozer as irritated; it should refer to the people.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: Choose the correct sentences: (i) The guests were treated to a lavish meal. (ii) They ate until they were full. (iii) That dinner party was talked about for a long time.
questions.explanation: All three sentences are grammatically correct and form a coherent sequence about the dinner party.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: Choose the correct sentences: (i) Ram was known for his eloquence. (ii) Ram was invited to speech on the meeting. (iii) At the last minute, he had to cancel the program.
questions.explanation: Sentences (i) and (iii) are correct. “Invited to speech on the meeting” in (ii) is not grammatical; it would be “invited to speak at the meeting.”
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: Choose the correct sentences: (i) The aeroplane glided smooth in the blue sky. (ii) The passengers leaned back in their seats. (iii) It was such a comfortable flight.
questions.explanation: Sentences (ii) and (iii) are correct. In (i), the adverb “smoothly” is required instead of the adjective “smooth.”
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: Choose the correct sentences: (i) John is such a good swimmer. (ii) He could swam in any sea. (iii) He once swam in the English Channel.
questions.explanation: Sentences (i) and (iii) are correct. After the modal “could,” the base form “swim,” not “swam,” is required in (ii).
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: Choose the correct sentences: (i) Isn't he the Principal of the school? (ii) I heard that he's a man of integrity. (iii) He combines strictness with approachability.
questions.explanation: All three sentences are grammatical: the question, the report of his integrity, and the statement about his balanced leadership.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: Choose the correct sentences: (i) Can you do me favor? (ii) Can you favor me? (iii) Can you do me this favor please?
questions.explanation: Sentences (ii) and (iii) are acceptable. Sentence (i) is missing the article in “do me a favor.”
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: Choose the correct sentences: (i) He told us a very interesting story. (ii) The interesting listeners were captivated. (iii) Nobody wanted the story to end.
questions.explanation: Sentences (i) and (iii) are correct. In (ii), “interesting listeners” should be “interested listeners.”
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: Choose the correct sentences: (i) How many books do you wish to buy? (ii) How many books did she wish to buy? (iii) You wish to buy books how many?
questions.explanation: Sentences (i) and (ii) use correct question word order. Sentence (iii) places “how many” incorrectly.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: Choose the correct sentences: (i) Jim was the monitor in class for five years. (ii) Jim was the class monitor for five years. (iii) Jim had been a class monitor for five years.
questions.explanation: All three statements are grammatically possible: “monitor in class” and “class monitor” are both usable descriptions, and the past perfect in (iii) is valid when referring to a prior period.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: Choose the correct sentences: (i) I've never seen a tiger at close range. (ii) I've never seen a tiger this close. (iii) I've never seen a tiger close up.
questions.explanation: All three expressions—“at close range,” “this close,” and “close up”—are acceptable ways to describe seeing a tiger nearby.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: Choose the correct sentences: (i) She's a famous actress of yesteryears. (ii) She's a famous actress yesterday. (iii) She was once a famous actress.
questions.explanation: Sentences (i) and (iii) are correct. “She's a famous actress yesterday” in (ii) is ungrammatical.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: Choose the correct sentences: (i) After the harvest, the farmer went to bed happy. (ii) The good harvest made the farmer happy. (iii) After the harvest, the farmer went happy to bed.
questions.explanation: Sentences (i) and (ii) are natural and grammatical. “Went happy to bed” in (iii) is not the usual grammatical placement.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: Choose the correct sentences: (i) The current is too strong to cross. (ii) The current is too wide to cross. (iii) The current is too powerful to cross.
questions.explanation: All three constructions can describe a watercourse/current that is too strong, too wide, or too powerful to cross. Each uses the valid pattern “too + adjective + to-infinitive.”
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: Choose the correct sentences: (i) The Sun is too heat today. (ii) The Sun is too hot today. (iii) The Sun is so hot today.
questions.explanation: Sentences (ii) and (iii) are correct. “Too heat” in (i) incorrectly uses the noun “heat” where the adjective “hot” is needed.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: Choose the correct sentences: (i) Don't you have anything better to do? (ii) Don't you have anything to do with your time? (iii) Don't you have anything useful to do?
questions.explanation: All three questions are grammatically formed. In (ii), “do with your time” asks what use or activity someone has for their time.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: Choose the correct sentences: (i) For heaven's sake, stop wasting your time! (ii) For heaven's sake, stop waste time! (iii) For heaven's sake, stop wasting time!
questions.explanation: Sentences (i) and (iii) are correct. After “stop,” the gerund “wasting” is required in this construction.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: Choose the correct sentences: (i) She's a strong, confident woman. (ii) She exudes confident. (iii) Her confidence is admired by many.
questions.explanation: Sentences (i) and (iii) are correct. “Exudes confident” is incorrect because the noun “confidence” is required.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: Choose the correct sentences: (i) Which pairs of shoes do you prefer? (ii) Which pair of shoes do you prefer? (iii) Which of these pairs do you prefer?
questions.explanation: All three questions are grammatical: they ask about multiple pairs, one pair, or a choice among a specified set of pairs.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: Choose the correct sentences: (i) The restaurant opens at all hours. (ii) The restaurant opens 24x7. (iii) The restaurant is opening at all times.
questions.explanation: Sentences (i) and (ii) express regular or continuous opening hours correctly. “Is opening at all times” is not idiomatic for a regular schedule.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: His most trusted friend proved to be a snake in the grass.
questions.explanation: A “snake in the grass” is a person who conceals hostile or treacherous intentions; “a hidden enemy” is the closest definition.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: You cannot have your cake and eat it too.
options: make the best of a situation
questions.explanation: The idiom means that one cannot retain two mutually incompatible advantages; “have it both ways” expresses that meaning.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: The cashier wiped the nose of his employer by presenting false bills.
questions.explanation: To “wipe someone’s nose” in this idiomatic use is to cheat or take advantage of them; “cheated” is the closest option.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: After the death of his father, the son played ducks and drakes with his inherited property.
questions.explanation: To play ducks and drakes with property means to squander or spend it recklessly; “spend lavishly” is the closest option.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: After his retirement, Mr. Dave is thinking of resting on his oars.
questions.explanation: “Rest on one’s oars” means to stop making efforts after a period of activity or success; “resting after hard work” is the closest option.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: Easy to shape in desired form
questions.explanation: Malleable means capable of being shaped or moulded into a desired form.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: Very pleasing to eat
questions.explanation: Luscious can describe food that is richly pleasing or delicious to eat.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: One who desires freedom from control, especially government control
questions.explanation: An anarchist advocates the absence or abolition of coercive government control.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: Beyond all power of destruction of time
questions.explanation: Imperishable means not liable to decay or be destroyed by the passage of time.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: Composed of elements highly diverse in character
questions.explanation: Heterogeneity denotes diversity or the condition of being composed of unlike elements. Strictly, the adjective matching the phrase is “heterogeneous”; the offered noun “heterogeneity” is the closest available option.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: Punctilious
questions.explanation: Punctilious means very attentive to detail and exact observance of rules; “meticulous” is its closest synonym.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: Mendacious
questions.explanation: Mendacious means lying or untruthful; “deceitful” is the closest synonym.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: Ameliorate
questions.explanation: Ameliorate means to make something better or improve it.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: Cursory
questions.explanation: Cursory means hasty or superficial, done without close attention; “casual” is the closest option.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: Implicate
questions.explanation: To implicate someone is to involve them in an act or matter, especially one that is wrong.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: Choose the antonym of 'Selfish' in the context of the passage.
questions.explanation: Selfless is the direct antonym of selfish because it describes concern for others rather than oneself.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: Choose the antonym of 'Comfortable' in the context of the passage.
questions.explanation: Uncomfortable is the direct opposite of comfortable.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: Choose the antonym of 'Important' in the context of the passage.
questions.explanation: Trivial means of little importance or significance, the opposite of important.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: Choose the antonym of 'Underestimate'.
questions.explanation: To overestimate is to estimate too highly, the opposite of underestimating.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: Choose the antonym of 'Decayed'.
questions.explanation: Thriving means growing or flourishing, the opposite of having decayed.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: Choose the meaning of 'Breeding place' in the context of the passage.
questions.explanation: In the passage, the home is called the breeding place of good or bad because it is a formative environment in which values and behaviour develop.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: Choose the meaning of 'Pander' in the context of the passage.
questions.explanation: To pander to someone’s wishes is to give in to or gratify their demands, often excessively.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: Choose the meaning of 'Symptom' in the context of the passage.
questions.explanation: A symptom is a sign or indication of an underlying condition or state.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.text: Choose the meaning of 'Society at large' in the context of the passage.
questions.explanation: “Society at large” means the wider or greater community beyond an individual family or neighbourhood.
questions.sourceName: MPSC Lower Division Assistant question booklet, Series I, examination dated 14 December 2024 (advertisement cycle 2023); exact uploaded PDF [LDA(OCT-2023].pdf checked page-by-page.

questions.explanation: Option C gives 8 ÷ 8 × 1 + 7 = 1 × 1 + 7 = 8, using the usual left-to-right rule for division and multiplication.

questions.text: Johnny walked 25 m towards South. Then he turned to his left and walked 20 m. He then turned to his left and walked 25 m. He again turned to his right and walked 15 m. At what distance is he from his starting point and in which direction?
questions.explanation: He walks 25 m south, 20 m east, 25 m north and 15 m east. The north–south movements cancel; the net displacement is 35 m east.

questions.text: Given below are two statements followed by two conclusions. Consider the statements true even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts. Statements: I. Health Insurance in India caters only to the rich. II. Health Insurance Sector should be regularized. Conclusions: I. Health Insurance Sector should be nationalized. II. Health Insurance is not required for the poor. Which conclusion follows?
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: Neither conclusion follows. The statements do not establish that the sector must be nationalised, nor that poor people do not need health insurance.

questions.text: Given below are three statements followed by two conclusions. Statements: I. All shoes are pens. II. Some pens are razors. III. Some razors are desks. Conclusions: I. Some desks are shoes. II. Some razors are shoes. Which conclusion(s) follow?
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusion I and II follow
questions.explanation: All shoes are pens, but the statements do not establish any overlap between shoes and razors or between shoes and desks. Neither conclusion is guaranteed.

questions.text: Danny introduced Wilburn as the son of the only brother of his father's wife. How is Wilburn related to Danny?
questions.explanation: The only brother of Danny’s father’s wife is Danny’s maternal uncle. The uncle’s son is Danny’s cousin.

questions.text: Select the related letters from the given alternatives: Bbc : cBB :: Llm : ?
questions.explanation: The letters are reversed and the resulting pattern has a lowercase first letter followed by two uppercase letters: Bbc → cBB, so Llm → mLL.

questions.text: If 1st January is a Friday, then what is the first day of the month of March in a leap year?
questions.explanation: January and February in a leap year have 31+29=60 days. 60 leaves a remainder of 4 when divided by 7; Friday + 4 days is Tuesday.

questions.text: Which is the smallest in value among the following numbers?
questions.explanation: Compare logarithms: log10(2²⁵⁰)≈75.26, log10(3¹⁵⁰)≈71.57, log10(5¹⁰⁰)≈69.90, and log10(4²⁰⁰)≈120.41. The smallest is 5¹⁰⁰, option C.
